turns.text:
## Findings

**Gross profit by quarter (basis: gross_profit metric, quantity times unit price less quantity times unit cost valid on sale date):**

| Product | Q1 2026 sales | Q1 gross profit | Q1 margin | Q2 2026 sales | Q2 gross profit | Q2 margin |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Insulated bottle | $12,000 | $6,000 | 50.0% | $12,000 | $4,800 | 40.0% |
| Field jacket | $10,000 | $4,000 | 40.0% | $10,000 | $3,400 | 34.0% |

Units sold and list prices were unchanged between quarters (both products held list price flat: bottle $30, jacket $50; sales volume was flat too). The entire margin decline came from the cost side.

## Why it fell

Both products are supplied by **Meridian Supply**, whose terms carry a volume break: 500 units per quarter across all Meridian products, and the tier a quarter's orders earn sets *next* quarter's unit cost (assertion 69188, supplier.terms). Meridian's tiered costs are:
- Insulated bottle (A-100): $15.00 at or above 500 units, $18.00 below.
- Field jacket (B-200): $30.00 at or above 500 units, $33.00 below.

Purchase orders placed with Meridian in Q1 2026 (Jan-Mar) totaled **470 units** (quarter_units_ordered metric), below the 500-unit break. That missed break set the unit cost for Q2: bottle unit cost stepped from $15.00 to $18.00 (+20%) effective 2026-04-01, and jacket unit cost stepped from $30.00 to $33.00 (+10%) effective 2026-04-01 (assertions 69243, 69245). With sales unchanged, that cost increase is the entire margin drop.

## What would restore it

The lever is purchasing volume, not price. Ordering at or above 500 units from Meridian in a quarter earns the lower tier for the *following* quarter. However, **Q2 2026 orders also came in at 480 units**, still under the 500-unit break, so on current form Q3 2026 will carry the same elevated costs ($18 / $33) unless Q2's shortfall is corrected before quarter end or Q3 orders are increased. Concretely: place Meridian purchase orders (across the insulated bottle, field jacket, and any other Meridian SKUs combined) totaling 500 units or more in a quarter to lock in $15.00/$30.00 unit costs for the quarter after. Per purchasing policy, a Meridian reorder up to $2,000 is pre-approved; if a larger top-up order is needed to clear the 500-unit line, confirm its total against that cap since amounts above $2,000 need owner approval. No price change is required to fix this; raising list prices is a separate lever and any change above 5% would need owner approval under pricing policy.

ANSWER: Insulated bottle gross profit was $6,000 in Q1 2026 (50.0% margin) and fell to $4,800 in Q2 (40.0%); field jacket gross profit was $4,000 in Q1 (40.0% margin) and fell to $3,400 in Q2 (34.0%). Sales volume and list prices were flat both quarters; the drop is entirely because Meridian Supply's volume-break terms (500 units/quarter across all Meridian products sets next quarter's cost) were missed in Q1 (only 470 units ordered), stepping unit costs up from $15 to $18 (bottle) and $30 to $33 (jacket) starting 2026-04-01. Q2 orders (480 units) also missed the break, so Q3 costs will stay elevated unless Meridian orders reach 500 units in a quarter; this is a purchasing fix, not a price change.
